open_items: The Water Conservation Tax rounding stage: 0.7150 or 0.7200. This is the only thing holding the city at Grade B. It is one field in a public PDF, not a missing document.
A private SP Services invoice is now reconciliation, not a blocker. The billing formula, the rounding order and a two-line arithmetic check all came from published sources.

components.name: Water Conservation Tax
components.rate_display: 50% of the water tariff — S$ 0.715 / m³ (PUB prints S$ 0.72)
components.source_precedence: statutory/official formula (50% of tariff, stated in the Annex A footnote) outranks the rounded presentation table in the same annex, which prints S$ 0.72
components.assumption_note: The rate is the official formula, 50% of the 1.43 tariff, which is 0.715. PUB's own Annex A prints 0.72 in a row labelled '(% of Tariff)'. Precedence puts the formula above the presentation table. SP's published sample bill prints rates to four decimal places and would show which is billed, but the Water Conservation Tax line is not in the text layer of the capture. If 0.72 is billed, the water supply bill becomes S$ 35.15 and the total S$ 52.97.
components.closes_with: A visual read of the Water Conservation Tax rate field in SP's published sample bill, or any official document printing that rate to four decimals. A private invoice is one way and no longer the only way.

components.name: U-Save rebate
components.exclusion_note: Rule 3.1. PUB states there are no rebates for households consuming below a given volume; U-Save is a targeted government utilities credit, not a universal automatic feature of this tariff.

shape_note: PUB blocks are monthly at 40 m3. The scenario resolves 15 m3 within each of twelve months, so the whole volume sits in the first block. PUB itself puts the average household at about 15 m3 a month and states that more than 96% of households stay below 40 m3.
grade_reason: Grade B on one disclosed assumption: the rounding stage of the Water Conservation Tax. Every other input is established from a published primary source — the rates and the 50% rule from PUB's media release Annex A, currency from SP's tariff page, the 9% GST from IRAS, and the billing formula and rounding order from SP's published sample bill, which the engine reconciles exactly on two of three lines at 23.7 m3. What remains is whether SP bills the Conservation Tax at 0.7150 or at the 0.7200 printed in Annex A. The two differ by S$ 0.08 on the standard bill: U = 0.233%, inside the 1% Grade B ceiling.

materiality.note: Bmin from the formula rate 0.715, Bmax from the printed 0.72. The spread is a rounding stage, not a disagreement between sources.

billing_formula.rate_precision: four decimal places as printed on the bill
billing_formula.line_rounding: each line amount rounded to cents
billing_formula.tax_order: GST computed per individual item and the items summed, not applied once to a grand total
billing_formula.note: Established from SP's own published sample bill, not from a private invoice. The engine already applied GST per stream group; at 15 m3 both readings give the same cents, and the documented rule is per item.

public_reconciliation.note: The same independent check Dubai has through its verified invoice, obtained here from a public document. The Water Conservation Tax line is not in the capture, so the reconciliation covers two of the three PUB components.

reference_connection.size: Domestic metered service — no connection-size parameter
reference_connection.designation: PUB's Annex A prices domestic water purely per cubic metre, and SP's published bill enumerates what PUB collects on a domestic account as water charges, NEWater charges, water conservation tax and waterborne tax. No standing or meter-size charge appears in either. The residential tariff has no size parameter to designate.

jurisdiction.note: City is a display layer. The observation belongs to jurisdiction x utility x service area x customer class x schedule x period.

continuity.note: SP Services is PUB's billing agent, and its tariff information page captured 17 August 2026 shows the 1 April 2025 rates as the ones being billed. The rates originate in PUB's media release of 27 September 2023, which announced a two-stage revision; the second stage is the tariff in force and there is no third. An announcement of a future revision would not close this record in any case — a future rate is not an observation — but the billing agent's current page is what shows the present one still being charged.
